patches.summary: Honor SL_API_KEY in addition to the press-default SYNDICATE_LINKS_BEARER_AUTH.
patches.reason: Syndicate Links docs and existing tooling (syndicate-links-mcp, SDKs, dashboard examples) all reference SL_API_KEY. The press generates the env var from the OpenAPI security scheme name; the human-readable canonical name diverges. Both are accepted to avoid breaking either path.
patches.validated_outcome: doctor and merchant list-programs succeed when only SL_API_KEY is set (live against api.syndicatelinks.co).

patches.summary: Remove the press-generated MCP server (cmd/syndicate-links-pp-mcp, internal/mcp/, manifest.json) and trim Makefile targets.
patches.reason: Syndicate Links already ships a hand-tuned MCP server (`syndicate-links-mcp` on npm, https://www.npmjs.com/package/syndicate-links-mcp) maintained alongside the API. Shipping a second auto-generated MCP server creates a maintenance fork and ambiguity for agents that discover both. The hand-tuned server has 7 tools shaped for the agent commerce use case; the press generated 52 thin endpoint mirrors. Two MCPs hurts; one focused one wins.
patches.validated_outcome: go build ./... succeeds; CLI works against live API.

patches.summary: Stop AuthHeader() from overwriting AuthSource that Load() set authoritatively; only fill it when empty.
patches.reason: Load() correctly distinguishes env:SL_API_KEY from env:SYNDICATE_LINKS_BEARER_AUTH and from config-file credentials, but AuthHeader() then unconditionally clobbered the label with env:SYNDICATE_LINKS_BEARER_AUTH on every call. doctor and auth status reported the wrong credential source for SL_API_KEY users. Fix preserves the Load()-set label and only fills AuthSource when it was empty (bypass-Load callers).
patches.validated_outcome: go test ./internal/cli ./internal/cliutil ./internal/store pass; the doctor/auth-status JSON now mirrors which env var actually supplied the key.

patches.summary: Tighten ~/.cache/syndicate-links-pp-cli/ to 0o700 dir / 0o600 files to match the config-file perm convention.
patches.reason: HTTP response cache files contain merchant program configs, conversion records, and balance data. They were written 0o644 in a 0o755 dir, world-readable on shared systems. Match the 0o600 config-file convention so cached commerce data is not exposed to other local users. Pre-existing files keep their old perms until next write; users wanting an immediate fix can `chmod -R go-rwx ~/.cache/syndicate-links-pp-cli`.
patches.validated_outcome: go build ./... clean; cache test suite passes; manual smoke confirms new cache files land 0o600 in a 0o700 dir.

patches.summary: Validate ListIDs() resourceType against a hardcoded allowlist of domain tables before SQL interpolation; everything else routes to the parameterized resources-table fallback.
patches.reason: ListIDs() interpolated resourceType straight into `SELECT id FROM %s` via fmt.Sprintf. Parameter binding doesn't work for table names, so for the domain-table path we validate the name against a known-good set (affiliate, merchant) before formatting. Anything outside the allowlist falls through to the already-parameterized `SELECT id FROM resources WHERE resource_type = ?` and never touches the formatted string. No actual exploit path today (call sites pass hardcoded values), but closes the pattern.
patches.validated_outcome: go test ./internal/store passes; domain-table reads of affiliate and merchant still work; arbitrary resource types correctly fall through to the parameterized fallback.
